record.original_question: Does every 2-edge-connected graph admit a nowhere-zero 5-flow?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.5 Every 2-edge-connected graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G=(V,E) be a finite undirected graph, possibly with multiple edges, that is 2-edge-connected (equivalently, bridgeless: G is connected and has no cut edge). Fix an arbitrary orientation of the edges of G, turning it into a directed graph. For a positive integer k, a nowhere-zero k-flow on G is an assignment f : E → {-(k-1), -(k-2), ..., -1, 1, 2, ..., k-1} of nonzero integers to the (oriented) edges such that at every vertex v ∈ V, the sum of f(e) over edges e directed into v equals the sum of f(e) over edges e directed out of v. (Whether such an f exists does not depend on the chosen orientation.)

Prove or disprove: every 2-edge-connected graph admits a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
artifact.status_search_result: Tutte's 5-flow conjecture (1954) remains open. The best general result is Seymour's theorem that every bridgeless graph admits a nowhere-zero 6-flow. Partial results are known for special classes, e.g. highly cyclically connected cubic graphs (Kochol and others), but the full conjecture is unresolved as of 2026.

status_evidence.snippet: Conjecture (Tutte): Every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 5-flow. Listed as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is listed as open.

status_evidence.snippet: Tutte's 5-flow Conjecture (1954): Every graph with no cut-edge has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an unresolved open problem.

status_evidence.title: Nowhere-zero flow - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Seymour proved that every bridgeless graph has a nowhere-zero 6-flow; Tutte's 5-flow conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Best known is 6-flow; 5-flow conjecture still open.
